newsitem.title: VIRGIN ISLANDS: Four found, one missing after Virgin Islands crash.
newsitem.headline: Four found, one missing after Virgin Islands crash.

text.p: The Coast Guard suspended its search for victims of a weekend commuter plane crash in the waters near the U.S. Virgin Islands that left one person presumed dead and another missing, a spokesman said on Monday.

The Air Sunshine twin-engine Cessna plane went down just south of St. Thomas on Saturday night after leaving St. Croix. Three people were rescued in the hours after the crash. Pilot Jeff James of Boca Raton, Florida, was plucked from the ocean and Frankie Bellot and Eugene Woodley, both of St. Croix, were found on a nearby island.

The other two who were aboard the plane were identified as James Fleming and Troy Donovan, both from St. Thomas. One of them was seen floating, presumably dead, without a life jacket, and the other had not been located by the time the search was suspended late Sunday after an all-day effort by boat and aircraft, the spokesman said.
"The search was suspended pending further developments," he said.

Air Sunshine Flight 319 left St. Croix at 7:15 p.m. EST (0015 GMT) en route to St. Thomas and nosedived into the sea 25 minutes later two 2 miles (3.2 km) south of St. Thomas after James had asked for clearance to land at Cyril King airport there.
James told the Coast Guard he had had problems with the aircraft's hydraulic system. The National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Aviation Administration began investigating immediately.
The crash was the third in five years for Air Sunshine.
The survivors told the Coast Guard one man, a non-swimmer, was not wearing a life jacket. They said they tried to assist him as they made their way to the island but were unable to save him.
